subject: Cross-cloud private offer: credit timing, commission escrow & reseller retention

Subject: Cross-cloud offer: credits & partner commission flow

Rishi — thanks again for the walkthrough today. A couple quick clarifications so our procurement and finance teams can draft the PO: we have a cross-cloud private offer that covers Azure + GCP usage over 12 months. Two specific asks: 1) timing for list-price credits / early-adopter credits (do credits apply at invoice date or as an offset on initial true-up?), and 2) how reseller commissions are handled if we switch to a different partner after year 1 (we need a retention/escrow mechanism).

I attached a high-level PO draft and a sample commission schedule from our reseller to show the expected waterfall. Can you confirm Redwood's position on credit timing and whether you can support an escrow for trailing commission for an initial 12-month term? Also cc'ing Tom from ResellerWave who will be on the invoice path.

Thanks,
Ella
Procurement Manager, Greencore AI
attachments: Greencore_PO_draft.pdf
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>

Date: Sun, 01 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cross-cloud offer: credits & partner commission flow

Ella — appreciate the clear summary and the PO draft. High level answers up-front: credits can be applied either as an invoice-level credit on month 1 or amortized across the first quarter depending on procurement preference; we typically attach credits to the invoice date of the first bill but can agree to an amortization schedule in the PO. For reseller commissions: we do support a time-bound escrow-style holdback for trailing commissions for cases where the partner is responsible for onboarding and retention — commonly 6–12 months.

I need to loop in finance and partner ops to confirm mechanics (ledger entries, whether Redwood or the marketplace holds the escrow, and how true-ups are handled). Naomi — can you review the attached commission schedule and advise whether we can do a marketplace-anchored escrow vs Redwood-managed escrow? Also flag any tax or revenue-recognition implications.

Ella / Tom — we aim to have a recommended approach by end of Tuesday.

Best,
Rishi
Director, Cloud Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: Greencore PO — credit timing & escrow options (need position)

Team — forwarding Greencore's ask (attached). Key commercial constraints: 1) Greencore expects an up-front early-adopter credit against initial invoice OR amortized credit; 2) reseller (ResellerWave / Tom) wants a guarantee that commissions will be preserved for 12 months even if Greencore moves to another partner. They propose a holdback in the PO and a schedule similar to the attached RI-commission-schedule-v1.xlsx.

Questions for ops/finance:
- Which approach minimizes our GAAP revenue recognition complexity? (invoice credit vs amortization)
- Can we offer a marketplace-managed escrow (typical for AWS private offers) or must Redwood run the escrow in our billing system? Pros/cons and timeline to support each.
- If Redwood runs the escrow, what are the required ledger changes and legal wording?

Ben — allocate any standard language we can include in the PO and the partner agreement for a 12-month trailing commission holdback. Irene — if the escrow sits on the marketplace side, are there any compliance or KYC steps we need from ResellerWave?

I'll synthesize responses to propose two commercial options to Greencore: Option A (invoice credit + marketplace escrow) and Option B (amortized credit + Redwood-managed escrow). Need responses by EOD Monday to hit Tuesday external deadline.

Thanks,
Rishi
From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.inference>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>, naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.inference>, irene_choi <irene@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 13:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Greencore PO — credit timing & escrow options (need position)

Short answers from deal desk / legal POV:
- Revenue recognition: invoice-level credit is clean operationally but means we recognize lower ARR at invoice issuance; amortization across Q1 is manageable but requires note in contract for deferral and will affect monthly revenue. For Greencore's size I recommend invoice credit where possible to keep accounting simple.
- Escrow mechanics: marketplace-managed escrow (preferred) — marketplace holds funds/credits and controls release on agreed milestones (makes reconciliation simpler for all parties). However, not all marketplaces support partner-level escrows uniformly; for Azure/GCP we can leverage private-offer flow or reseller pass-through if ResellerWave already has a marketplace contract.
- Redwood-managed escrow: feasible but operational overhead (legal wording, separate escrow ledger, weekly reconciliations). Can be built but needs 3–4 weeks lead time and legal sign-off.

Suggested language snippet for PO: "A trailing commission holdback of X% of partner-reported commission will be retained for 12 months and released upon confirmation of continued customer coverage or refund obligation as outlined in Appendix A." I'll draft precise wording and attach.

Ben
From: Ella Zhang <ella@greencore.ai>

Rishi / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the options. Greencore prefers Option A (invoice-level credit + marketplace-managed escrow) if we can confirm marketplace support for partner escrows on Azure + GCP private offers. Tom, can ResellerWave confirm marketplace capability and whether they can route the commission through the marketplace so the holdback is enforced by the platform?

If marketplace-managed escrow is not available, Greencore is prepared to accept a Redwood-managed escrow provided we get standard wording and a reconciliation cadence. Please send the PO with the chosen language (Ben's snippet is helpful) and the DocuSign link for signatures. We will aim to finalize the PO this week.

Best,
Ella
